name: LOFAR (Low-Frequency Array), core at Exloo
description: A radio telescope of thousands of simple dipole antennas grouped in stations, with its core near Exloo and stations across Europe. It works at low frequencies (10 to 240 MHz) and is operated by ASTRON.
highlights: It was officially opened on 12 June 2010 by Queen Beatrix.
As of 2019 it had 52 stations, 38 of them in the Netherlands.
In February 2021 it released a high-resolution image of 25,000 active supermassive black holes covering four percent of the northern sky.
